implementation.name: Salesforce Platform Apex
implementation.version_scope: Hosted Apex anonymous execution; organization and API version specific.

sources.label: Salesforce Apex platform and console tutorial

fit.text: Implement business logic around Salesforce records and events; execution is on the Salesforce Platform.

prerequisites.text: Learn classes and collections plus the organization data model; try code in a development organization.

execution.text: Save classes on the server or execute an anonymous block in the Developer Console.

behavior.text: Strong typing and transactional database access coexist with multitenant resource limits.

tooling.text: Developer Console supplies anonymous execution and logs; Apex includes unit testing and coverage facilities.

maintenance.text: Custom code targets an API version, which must be considered when changing organization behavior.

costs.text: The workflow needs an appropriate Salesforce organization; the tutorial does not establish production subscription pricing.

example.run_instructions: Choose Debug > Open Execute Anonymous Window in a development organization's Developer Console. Execute this block and inspect its log with Debug Only selected.
example.expected_result: The debug log contains 12; timestamps and prefixes vary.

licenses.scope: Hosted organization service, not a redistributable compiler grant.
licenses.notice: The instructional page does not establish an SPDX licence; the applicable organization service agreement is separate.

implementation.name: AppleScript 2 on macOS
implementation.version_scope: Archived language guide and current Script Editor workflow; application dictionaries are version specific.

fit.text: Automate scriptable macOS applications and combine workflows; each application exposes its own command vocabulary.

prerequisites.text: Use macOS and inspect a target application dictionary before scripting its commands.

execution.text: Compile and run in Script Editor; the dialog example needs no separately targeted application.

behavior.text: Application-directed commands are Apple events; application support determines the available operations.

tooling.text: Script Editor provides editing, execution and application-dictionary inspection.

maintenance.text: Older syntax can remain usable, but newer features and application commands require compatible versions.

costs.text: Apple product use follows its applicable agreement, which may differ from an online agreement version.

example.run_instructions: Paste into a new macOS Script Editor document, compile and click Run.
example.expected_result: A dialog displays PLLDN and an OK button.

licenses.scope: AppleScript supplied with the installed macOS product.
licenses.notice: No open-source SPDX expression is asserted for the installed host; read its applicable Apple agreement.

implementation.name: Anarki Arc on Racket
implementation.version_scope: Community Anarki fork; explicitly not guaranteed compatible with upstream Arc.

sources.label: Anarki runtime, development and compatibility README

fit.text: Explore Lisp macros and interactive application code through the Anarki fork.

prerequisites.text: Install the documented Racket prerequisite and sha package; learn prefix expressions and function definitions.

execution.text: Start arc.sh or the documented Windows launcher, then evaluate expressions at the Arc prompt.

behavior.text: Functions and macros use Lisp expressions; the tutorial shows defining abstractions in the running environment.

tooling.text: The repository includes built-in help, tests and a News application; Racket interoperation is available.

maintenance.text: Anarki explicitly permits upstream incompatibilities; inspect incompatibilities and preserve application data when migrating.

costs.text: The core copyright file grants Artistic-2.0 use; bundled applications and Racket have their own component scope.

example.run_instructions: Start the Anarki REPL as documented, then enter both forms or load double.arc with (load "double.arc").

licenses.scope: Named implementation only; dependencies and generated applications require separate review.
licenses.notice: Retain the implementation license and relevant notices when redistributing it.

implementation.name: Eclipse AspectJ compiler and weaver
implementation.version_scope: Code-style AspectJ aspects compiled by ajc; Java/runtime compatibility depends on the selected AspectJ release.

sources.label: AspectJ adoption and cross-cutting behavior guide
AspectJ ajc compiler and runtime options

fit.text: Express tracing or other behavior across selected Java join points; broad pointcuts also broaden the affected code.

prerequisites.text: Know Java before learning pointcuts, advice and weaving.

execution.text: ajc compiles or weaves aspects with Java classes; execution requires the documented AspectJ runtime on the Java classpath.

behavior.text: Advice runs at matched join points, so changing a pointcut can change behavior across multiple classes.

tooling.text: ajc exposes source, classpath and weaving options; preserve compiler messages that explain matched or unmatched code.

maintenance.text: Introduce aspects incrementally and inspect their effects when application structure changes.

costs.text: The implementation has EPL-2.0 terms; linked Java dependencies and runtime distribution need component review.

example.run_instructions: Compile Trace.aj with the installed ajc. Run class Trace with the compiled directory and the selected distribution's aspectjrt.jar on the Java classpath.
example.expected_result: The program prints before, then PLLDN.

licenses.scope: Named implementation only; dependencies and generated applications require separate review.
licenses.notice: Retain the implementation license and relevant notices when redistributing it.

implementation.name: NASM x86-64 ELF assembler on Linux
implementation.version_scope: NASM Intel syntax, ELF64 output and Linux x86-64 syscall ABI; not other CPUs or operating systems.

sources.label: NASM assembly syntax and instruction operands

fit.text: Write processor-specific routines with direct register and memory control; this profile targets only x86-64 Linux.

prerequisites.text: Learn instruction operands and registers, then the target object format and calling conventions.

execution.text: Assemble to an ELF64 object, link it into a Linux executable and execute it on the matching architecture.

behavior.text: The example puts syscall number 60 in eax and its exit argument in edi before invoking syscall.

tooling.text: NASM selects object formats explicitly; a linker completes this standalone executable.

maintenance.text: A different OS, object format or CPU changes the interface; retain those target choices with the source.

costs.text: NASM has BSD-2-Clause terms; the assembler licence does not determine the licence of your source program.

example.code:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov eax, 60
    mov edi, 42
    syscall
example.run_instructions: On x86-64 Linux, assemble with nasm -f elf64 exit.asm -o exit.o, link using ld exit.o -o example, then run ./example and inspect its exit status.
example.expected_result: No text is printed; the process exits with status 42.

licenses.component: NASM x86-64 ELF assembler on Linux
licenses.scope: Named implementation only; dependencies and generated applications require separate review.
licenses.notice: Retain the implementation license and relevant notices when redistributing it.

implementation.name: AutoHotkey v2
implementation.version_scope: Version 2 Windows scripting; version 1 syntax and migration require separate handling.

fit.text: Create Windows hotkeys and desktop automation; window behavior remains tied to the automated application.

prerequisites.text: Install AutoHotkey v2 and learn function-call syntax before using older script examples.

execution.text: Run a .ahk file with the v2 interpreter; hotkeys keep scripts available for their trigger.

behavior.text: Hotkey declarations attach script actions to key combinations; ordinary function calls perform the work.

tooling.text: The distribution supports script execution and self-contained compiled-script builds; source builds use native C++ tools.

maintenance.text: Version 1 and version 2 have different script support; preserve the required version when sharing a script.

costs.text: Core AutoHotkey source permits GPL-2.0-or-later; bundled PCRE and redistributed components require their separate notices.

example.run_instructions: Open hello.ahk with AutoHotkey v2, then press Ctrl+Alt+H. Exit the script from its tray menu when finished.

licenses.scope: Core implementation covered by the cited source-header grant; separately marked libraries and dependencies are excluded.
licenses.notice: The core header expressly permits GPL version 2 or later; bundled PCRE has separate notices.

implementation.name: AutoIt v3
implementation.version_scope: Windows AutoIt v3 scripting and MsgBox function; automation depends on the target application.

fit.text: Automate Windows controls, keystrokes and administrative desktop tasks using BASIC-like syntax.

prerequisites.text: Install AutoIt on Windows and distinguish its scripting syntax from other BASIC dialects.

execution.text: Run a .au3 script through AutoIt; the toolchain also supports standalone compiled scripts.

behavior.text: MsgBox displays text and returns a button result; flags choose its buttons and appearance.

tooling.text: AutoIt includes an interpreter, compiler and tools for inspecting Windows controls.

maintenance.text: UI automation depends on the chosen windows and controls; review identifiers when the application changes.

costs.text: The EULA allows commercial use and distribution under its conditions, but prohibits reverse engineering the product.

example.run_instructions: Save hello.au3 and run it with the installed AutoIt v3 interpreter on Windows.
example.expected_result: A message box titled Example displays PLLDN.

licenses.scope: AutoIt software product under its custom EULA; generated scripts have a separately described scope.
licenses.notice: The EULA permits commercial scripts and specifies product redistribution notices; it is not mapped to an SPDX open-source identifier.

implementation.name: GNU Awk (gawk)
implementation.version_scope: Basic pattern-action and field-processing workflow; GNU extensions are not automatically portable to other awk implementations.

fit.text: Process text records and fields with small pattern-action scripts; field separation must match the input format.

prerequisites.text: Learn records, field numbers, regular expressions and shell quoting before combining pipelines.

execution.text: Run gawk with -f and a source file; ordinary rules execute for each input record.

behavior.text: BEGIN and END run at startup and termination; an empty pattern applies to every record.

tooling.text: GNU Awk documents execution profiling and counts for patterns, rules and functions.

maintenance.text: GNU-specific directives and extensions need checking before moving code to another awk implementation.

costs.text: The accessed official manual excerpts establish behavior but not an exact licence expression for a selected compiler distribution.

example.run_instructions: With gawk installed, save input.txt containing 'apple 2' and 'pear 4' on separate lines. Run gawk -f sum.awk input.txt.

licenses.scope: Exact gawk distribution licence not established by the accessed manual excerpts.
licenses.notice: Inspect that release's COPYING and file headers; the manual's own licence is not substituted for the executable licence.

implementation.name: FreeBASIC in QB compatibility mode
implementation.version_scope: A concrete QuickBASIC-compatible learning path; not a specification for every historical BASIC dialect.

sources.label: FreeBASIC compiler, toolchain and component licenses
FreeBASIC dialect selection and compatibility limits

fit.text: Small console exercises and revisiting QuickBASIC-style code. Compatibility mode does not accept every dialect or every QB program.

prerequisites.text: Start with expressions, PRINT and control flow; select the QB dialect before importing older examples.

execution.text: fbc compiles .bas files to native executables; select -lang qb for this example.

behavior.text: QB mode restricts newer FreeBASIC features. Dialect differences matter when moving old code.

tooling.text: Use a text editor and fbc; the compiler relies on separate assembler/linker tooling.

maintenance.text: Test old source against the chosen dialect; switch to fb deliberately when adopting newer features.

costs.text: Compiler and linked runtime have different redistribution terms; inspect platform dependencies too.

example.run_instructions: With FreeBASIC installed, run fbc -lang qb hello.bas; run ./hello on Unix-like systems or .\hello.exe on Windows.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN followed by a newline.

licenses.scope: fbc compiler; distinct from linked runtime components.
licenses.notice: Distribution must follow the compiler's own license.

licenses.scope: libfb/libfbmt and libfbgfx/libfbgfxmt: LGPL version 2 or later with a custom static-linking exception.
licenses.notice: The exception has conditions for independent modules and modified libraries. No exact SPDX exception identifier is established here; inspect the full grant and other linked libraries.

implementation.name: CBQN interpreter
implementation.version_scope: CBQN command-line workflow; selected build flags and architecture affect the resulting interpreter.

sources.label: CBQN build, execution and component licensing

fit.text: Express arithmetic over arrays with BQN notation; CBQN documents implementation-specific limits separately.

prerequisites.text: Learn symbolic function notation; use an installed CBQN or satisfy its C-toolchain build requirements.

execution.text: Run a .bqn file with CBQN or enter expressions in its REPL.

behavior.text: Arithmetic functions extend to array arguments according to BQN's documented rules.

tooling.text: CBQN provides a REPL; optional line editing and foreign-function support depend on build configuration.

maintenance.text: Native CPU-specific optimization can reduce portability; rebuilding bootstrap bytecode must track interpreter updates.

costs.text: CBQN offers several core licensing choices; listed sorting, number-formatting and REPL components carry separate terms.

example.run_instructions: Execute ./BQN sum.bqn from an installed or built CBQN distribution.

licenses.scope: One offered choice for CBQN core files, excluding third-party exceptions listed in its README.
licenses.notice: The README offers alternative core licences; review listed MIT, Apache/Boost and optional REPL components separately.
